accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let I be a complete intersection ideal in the polynomial ring K[x1, ..., xn], where n is arbitrary. Must the Artinian quotient K[x1, ..., xn]/I always have the weak Lefschetz property, and does it perhaps always have the strong Lefschetz property as well?

evidence.quote: Question 2.1. Does every complete intersection ideal I ⊆ K[x1, . . . , xn], in any number of variables, has the WLP (or even the SLP)?

accepted.question_text: Does every height-three complete intersection have the strong Lefschetz property? More generally, does the same hold for complete intersections of larger height, for example Artinian complete intersections of height four?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. Does every height three complete intersection has the SLP? Is this true for complete intersections of larger height, e.g., Artinian height four?

accepted.question_text: Let I be a complete intersection in K[x1, ..., xn] generated by homogeneous polynomials all of the same degree d, and suppose the quotient K[x1, ..., xn]/I has the same monomial basis as the monomial complete intersection K[x1, ..., xn]/(x1^d, x2^d, ..., xn^d). Does K[x1, ..., xn]/I satisfy the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.3. Let I ⊆ K[x1, . . . , xn] be a complete intersection generated by homogeneous polynomials of uniform degree d ∈ N. Further assume that K[x1, . . . , xn]/I has the same monomial basis as K[x1, . . . , xn]/(x^d_1, x^d_2, . . . , x^d_n). Does K[x1, . . . , xn]/I satisfy the SLP?

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer d >= 2. For each n, let p_{n,d}(t) = Product_{i=1}^n (1 + t^i + ... + t^{i(d-1)}), equivalently the generating function for partitions of integers at most (d-1)n(n+1)/2 having at most n parts with each part repeated at most d-1 times. Are the coefficients of p_{n,d}(t) unimodal for all sufficiently large n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.4 (Almkvist ’85). For every fixed d ≥ 2, the polynomial pn,d(t) has unimodal coefficients for n sufficiently large.

Let pn,d(t) be the generating function for the number of partitions of integers smaller than or equal to (d−1)n(n+ 1)/2 with at most n parts and each part repeated at most d − 1 times. It is known that pn,d(t) = Π^n_{i=1}(1 + t^i + · · · + t^{i(d−1)}).

accepted.question_text: For integers n, d >= 1, let e_i(x1, ..., xn) denote the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial and let hat{e}_i = e_i(x1^d, ..., xn^d). Consider the non-standard graded Artinian complete intersection A(n, d) = K[e1, ..., en]/(hat{e}_1, ..., hat{e}_n). For which pairs (n, d) does A(n, d) have the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. For which pairs (n, d) does the ring A(n, d) have the SLP?

Given integers n, d ≥ 1, let ei = ei(x1, . . . , xn) be the ith elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables x1, . . . , xn, and let ˆei = ei(x^d_1, . . . , x^d_n) be the ith elementary symmetric polynomials in the variables raised to the dth powers x^d_1, . . . , x^d_n. ... Consequently, the quotient ring A(n, d) = K[e1,...,en]/(ˆe1,...,ˆen) is a (non-standard) graded Artinian complete intersection.

accepted.question_text: Do all Artinian Gorenstein algebras of codimension three have the weak Lefschetz property, or even the strong Lefschetz property? If not, can one characterize which codimension-three Artinian Gorenstein algebras do have these properties?

evidence.quote: Question 2.6. Do all Artinian codimension three Gorenstein algebras have the WLP (or even the SLP)? If not, can one characterize those which do?

accepted.question_text: Let A = direct sum_{i=0}^c A_i be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra over a field whose characteristic is zero or greater than c, with embedding dimension n. Suppose the symmetric group S_n acts on A by permuting the variables. Must A have the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.7. Let A = ⊕^c_{i=0} Ai be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra over a field of characteristic zero or greater than c with embedding dimension n. Suppose that the symmetric group Sn acts on A by permutation of the variables. Does A have the SLP?

accepted.question_text: Let S = C[x0, ..., xn], let f be a homogeneous polynomial of degree d whose hypersurface V(f) in projective space P^n is smooth, let J_f be the Jacobian ideal generated by the partial derivatives of f, and let M(f) = S/J_f be the graded Milnor or Jacobian algebra. Does M(f) always have the weak Lefschetz property, and does it perhaps always have the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.8. Does M(f) have the WLP (or the SLP) for any homogeneous form f ∈ C[x0, . . . , xn] with V (f) ⊂ P^n smooth?

Let S = C[x0, . . . , xn] be the polynomial ring in n+1 variables with coefficients in C and let f ∈ S be a homogeneous polynomial of degree d whose corresponding hypersurface V = V (f) = {x ∈ P^n : f(x) = 0} in P^n is smooth. Let Jf be the Jacobian ideal of f, generated by the partial derivatives fi of f with respect to xi for i = 0, . . . , n. The graded algebra M(f) = S/Jf is called the graded Milnor (or Jacobian) algebra of f.

accepted.question_text: Fix positive integers n and t. Determine, or at least bound, the smallest degree d for which there exists a monomial level algebra in n variables of type t whose last syzygy module is generated in degree d and for which the algebra fails the weak Lefschetz property.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9. Let n and t be positive integers. Find or bound the minimal degree d such that there exists a monomial level algebra in n variables of type t whose last syszygy module is generated in degree d and fails the WLP.

accepted.question_text: Let I be a monomial ideal such that the quotient R/I has the weak Lefschetz property in characteristic zero. For which characteristics of the ground field does the same quotient fail to have the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.10. Let I be a monomial ideal such that R/I has the WLP in characteristic zero. What are the field characteristics in which R/I fails to have the WLP?

accepted.question_text: Let R = K[x1, ..., xm], let L1, ..., Lr be general linear forms in R, and let I = (x1^d, ..., xm^d, L1^d, ..., Lr^d). For which triples (m, d, r) does the Artinian algebra R/I fail the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.12. Let R = K[x1, . . . , xm]. Let L1, . . . , Lr ∈ R be general linear forms, and let I = ⟨x^d_1, . . . , x^d_m, L^d_1, . . . , L^d_r⟩. Determine for which values of m, d and r the algebra R/I fails the WLP

accepted.question_text: A square-free monomial ideal I ⊆ S = K[x0, ..., xn] is called a square-free Gotzmann ideal when it can be written as m1(x_i : i in J1) + m1m2(x_i : i in J2) + ... + m1...ms(x_i : i in Js) for square-free monomials m1, ..., ms and pairwise disjoint subsets J1, ..., Js of {0, 1, ..., n}. Which square-free Gotzmann ideals satisfy the weak Lefschetz property, and do any Artinian reductions of Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes satisfy the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.13. Which square free Gotzmann ideals satisfy the WLP? Do (some) Artinian reductions of Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes satisfy the WLP?

A square-free monomial ideal I ⊆ S = K[x0, · · · xn] is called Gotzmann ideal if and only if I = m1(xi : i ∈ J1) + m1m2(xi : i ∈ J2) + · · · + m1m2 · · · ms(xi : i ∈ Js) for some square-free monomials m1, . . . , ms and pairwise disjoint subsets J1, . . . , Js of {0, 1, . . . , n}.

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a reduced arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in projective space P^n over a field of characteristic zero. Does a general Artinian reduction of the coordinate ring of Z always have the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. Does a general Artinian reduction of a reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in P^n has the WLP (provided that the characteristic of the underlying field equals zero)?

accepted.question_text: For a reduced arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in projective space over a field of characteristic zero, is its h-vector always unimodal?

evidence.quote: Question 3.2. Is the h-vector of every reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points unimodal (provided that the characteristic of the underlying field equals zero)?

accepted.question_text: Does every irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^4 admit an Artinian reduction that has the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Do all irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in P^4 have an Artinian reduction that has the SLP?

accepted.question_text: Besides the currently known examples, are there other arrangements of distinct complex projective lines with the property that no point is incident to exactly two of the lines?

evidence.quote: Question 3.4. Are there other complex line arrangements having no points where exactly two lines meet?

accepted.question_text: A finite set Z in P^n is called geproci if its image under projection from a general point P to a fixed hyperplane H is a complete intersection. In P^3, a set Z is called (a, b)-geproci if its projection is the transverse intersection of curves C_{a,P} and C_{b,P} of degrees a <= b. Find a non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set for which neither C_{a,P} nor C_{b,P} is an unexpected curve, or prove that no such set exists.

evidence.quote: A finite set Z ⊆ P^n is said to be geproci if its image ZP under projection from a general point P to a fixed hyperplane H is a complete intersection. ... In this case, we say Z is (a, b)-geproci if Zp is the transverse intersection of a curve Ca,P of degree a with a curve Cb,P of degree b where a ≤ b (hence |Z| = ab).
Problem 3.6. Find a non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set, where Ca,P and Cb,P is not unexpected, or show that no such example exists.

accepted.question_text: Is every non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set forced to contain three collinear points, or can one construct a counterexample?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Prove or disprove (by giving a counterexample) that every non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set has a subset of 3 collinear points.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a geproci set in linearly general position, or can one prove that no linearly general geproci set exists?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.8. Find an example of a linearly general geproci set, or show that no such example exists.

accepted.question_text: Suppose two geproci point sets have isomorphic matroids. Must they be projectively equivalent? More generally, is the property of being geproci determined purely by the associated matroid, so that any point set with a matroid isomorphic to that of a geproci set is itself geproci?

evidence.quote: Question 3.9. Are geproci sets with isomorphic matroids projectively equivalent? Is being geproci a property of the associated matroids, i.e., is a set of points whose matroid is isomorphic to the matroid of a geproci set, geproci itself?

accepted.question_text: Let Delta be a balanced simplicial (d-1)-sphere on vertex set [n], meaning there is a coloring c:[n]->[d] with c(u) != c(v) on every edge. Let Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d be the colored linear system of parameters defined by theta_i = sum_{c(v)=i} x_v. Does the Artinian reduction S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) always have the strong Lefschetz property, or at least the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Let ∆ be a balanced simplicial (d − 1)-sphere and Θ = θ1, . . . , θd be a colored linear system of parameters of ∆. Does the algebra S/(I∆ + (Θ)) have the SLP (or WLP)?

A simplicial complex on [n] of dimension (d − 1) is said to be (completely) balanced if there exists a function c : [n] → [d] such that c(v) ≠ c(u) for all edges {u, v} ∈ ∆. ... If ∆ is balanced, then it is known that the sequence of linear forms θ1, . . . , θd defined by θi = Σ_{c(v)=i} xv forms a linear system of parameters of ∆, called a colored linear system of parameters of ∆.

accepted.question_text: Let Delta be a centrally symmetric simplicial sphere, so Delta admits a fixed-point-free involution alpha on its vertex set, and let Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d be a linear system of parameters chosen generically from S^- = {f in S : alpha(f) = -f}. With respect to the linear form w = x1 + ... + xn, does the Artinian reduction S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) always have the strong or weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. Let ∆ be a centrally symmetric simplicial sphere and let Θ = θ1, . . . , θd be a linear system of parameters for K[∆] that has been generically taken from S−. Does the algebra S/(I∆ + (Θ)) have the SLP or WLP with respect to the linear form w = x1 + · · · + xn?

A simplicial complex ∆ on vertex set [n] is said to be centrally symmetric (cs, for short) if it admits a free Z/2Z-action, that is, there is a fixed-point free involution α : [n] → [n] with ∆ = {α(F) | F ∈ ∆}. For such a simplicial complex, one can choose a linear system of parameters Θ = θ1, . . . , θd from S− = {f ∈ S | α(f) = −f}, where α(xv) is defined to be xα(v).

accepted.question_text: Let Delta be a flag simplicial (d-1)-sphere with d >= 5, let Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d be a generic linear system of parameters, and let w and w' be additional generic linear forms. Is the multiplication map by w' from degree 1 to degree 2 in S/(I_Delta + (Theta, w)) always injective?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Let ∆ be a flag simplicial (d − 1)-sphere with d ≥ 5, let Θ = θ1, . . . , θd be a generic linear system of parameters and let w, w′ be additional generic linear forms. Is it true that the multiplication ×w′ : (S/(I∆ + (Θ, w))1 → (S/(I∆ + (Θ, w))2 is injective?
Flag spheres A simplicial complex ∆ is said to be flag if I∆ has no generators of degree ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Cohen-Macaulay CW complex Gamma such that, for every choice of linear system of parameters Theta, the Artinian reduction S/(I_{sd(Gamma)} + (Theta)) of the Stanley-Reisner ring of the barycentric subdivision sd(Gamma) fails the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 4.5. Is there a Cohen–Macaulay CW complex Γ such that S/(Isd(Γ) + (Θ)) does not have the weak Lefschetz property for any linear system of parameters Θ?

accepted.question_text: Besides barycentric subdivisions, are there other classes of simplicial complexes for which the corresponding Artinian reductions satisfy the same almost Lefschetz pattern described earlier: for a generic linear system of parameters Theta and a generic linear form w, the maps w^{d-2k-1}: (S/(I + (Theta)))_k -> (S/(I + (Theta)))_{d-1-k} are injective for k <= (d-1)/2, and the maps w^{d-2k-1}: (S/(I + (Theta)))_{k+1} -> (S/(I + (Theta)))_{d-k} are surjective for k <= (d-1)/2?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. Are there other classes of simplicial complexes (different from barycentric subdivisions) that satisfy (i) and (ii) above?

(i) ×w^{d−2k−1} : (S/(Isd(Γ) + (Θ)))_k → (S/(Isd(Γ) + (Θ)))_{d−1−k} is injective for k ≤ (d − 1)/2; (ii) ×w^{d−2k−1} : (S/(Isd(Γ) + (Θ)))_{k+1} → (S/(Isd(Γ) + (Θ)))_{d−k} is surjective for k ≤ (d − 1)/2.

accepted.question_text: Let F1, ..., Fs be homogeneous forms of degree d in variables y1, ..., yn, let x1, ..., xs be new variables, and consider the Artinian Gorenstein algebra whose Macaulay inverse system is generated by sum_i x_i^e F_i. Determine, for general values of e and for specific choices of the forms F_i, when this Gorenstein algebra has the weak Lefschetz property and when it has the strong Lefschetz property.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.7. To determine whether the Gorenstein algebra given by Σ x^e_iFi has the WLP and/or the SLP.

In terms of Macaulay inverse systems, we can construct the idealization of the canonical module of an Artinian level algebra with inverse system ⟨F1, F2, . . . , Fs⟩ as the Gorenstein algebra with inverse system ⟨Σ xiFi⟩ where x1, x2, . . . , xs are new variables. Here the forms F1, . . . , Fs are assumed to be homogeneous of degree d in variables y1, y2, . . . , yn. Preliminary studies of the Gorenstein algebra given by ⟨Σ x^e_iFi⟩ show that for e ≥ d it satisfies the WLP for any forms Fi while for e < d we have examples failing the WLP and examples satisfying the WLP.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a graded module over a graded Artinian algebra A. Is the generic Jordan type P_M always equal to the generic linear Jordan type P_{1,M} when the Hilbert function H(A) is not unimodal or when the generic Jordan type is not the conjugate partition of the Hilbert function? More generally, under what conditions on M and A does one have P_M = P_{1,M}?
accepted.context_brief: Generic versus generic linear Jordan type

evidence.quote: Question 5.1. Is this equality still true when H(A) is not unimodal, or when the generic Jordan type is not the conjugate partition of the Hilbert function? More generally, under which conditions on a graded module M over a graded Artinian algebra A do their generic and generic linear Jordan types satisfy PM = P1,M?
In particular, when M is a graded module over an Artinian algebra A we define the generic linear Jordan type P1,M as the Jordan type Pℓ,M for a generic linear form ℓ ∈ A1.

accepted.question_text: For which non-unimodal Hilbert functions H that occur for graded Artinian algebras A can one find a pair (A, ell) with H(A) = H such that the Jordan type and Jordan degree type of A agree with the contiguous Jordan type and contiguous Jordan-degree type determined by H?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2. For which (non-unimodal) Hilbert functions H occurring for graded Artinian algebras A, can we find pairs (A, ℓ) with H(A) = H and the Jordan type and Jordan degree types of A agree with the contiguous Jordan or Jordan-degree type of H?
When the Hilbert function H of a graded Artin module is non-unimodal, we can define a contiguous-Jordan type Pc,ℓ(H), and a contiguous-Jordan degree type Pc,deg,ℓ(H): using the bar graph of H(M).

accepted.question_text: Let A = R/I be a standard graded Artinian algebra and let in(I) be the initial ideal of I for a fixed monomial order. How does the generic Jordan degree type of A compare with that of the quotient R/in(I)? In particular, can there exist a pair (A, ell) whose Jordan degree type cannot occur for any pair (A', ell') in which A' is defined by a monomial ideal?

evidence.quote: Question 5.3. How does the generic Jordan degree type of a standard graded Artinian algebra A = R/I behave under projection to the quotient R/in(I)? Is there a pair (A, ℓ), where A is a standard graded Artinian algebra and ℓ ∈ A1, such that the Jordan degree type Pdeg,ℓ,A cannot occur for a pair (A′, ℓ′), if A′ is defined by a monomial ideal?

accepted.question_text: Determine the Hilbert function sequences H for non-graded Artinian algebras such that the family Z(H) of all algebras with Hilbert function H has several irreducible components whose general points share the same generic Jordan type but differ in one of the refined Jordan-type invariants such as sequential Jordan type, Loewy sequential Jordan type, or double sequential Jordan type.

evidence.quote: Question 5.4. Determine Hilbert function sequences H for non-graded Artinian algebras such that the family Z(H) of all algebras with Hilbert function H has several irreducible components Ξ1,Ξ2- whose general elements have the same generic Jordan type, but which differ in one of the refined invariants?
Lately, some refinements of Jordan type have been introduced for non-graded Artinian algebras: namely sequential Jordan type, Loewy sequential Jordan type, or double sequential Jordan type.

accepted.question_text: Given an exact sequence of finite A-modules 0 -> L -> M -> N -> 0, how are the generic Jordan types of L, M, and N related? Under what hypotheses can one obtain an additive relation between them? Can analogous comparison or additivity statements also be established for Jordan degree type in the graded case and for sequential, Loewy sequential, or double sequential Jordan type in the non-graded case?

evidence.quote: Question 5.5. Let 0 → L → M → N → 0 be an exact sequence of finite modules over A. How can we compare the generic Jordan types PL, PM, and PN ? Under what conditions could we have additivity PM = PL + PN , in a suitable sense for the Jordan types? The same question can be extended to Jordan degree type, in the graded case, or to sequential Jordan type, Loewy sequential Jordan type, or double sequential Jordan type, in the non graded case.

accepted.question_text: For families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras that fail the weak Lefschetz property, determine the number of parts in their generic linear Jordan types. More generally, for a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra that fails the strong Lefschetz property, determine its generic linear Jordan type.
accepted.context_brief: Jordan types for graded AG algebras

evidence.quote: Question 5.7. Determine the number of parts of generic linear Jordan types for the families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras failing the WLP. More generally, determine the generic linear Jordan type for a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra that fails the SLP.

accepted.question_text: Given a sequence H that occurs as the Hilbert function of a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra, which Jordan types or Jordan degree types are compatible with that Hilbert function?

evidence.quote: Question 5.8. Given a sequence H that can occur as the Hilbert function of a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra, can we find potential Jordan types or Jordan degree types?

accepted.question_text: Fix a Hilbert function H that occurs for a codimension-two complete intersection algebra. Can one determine all pairs of Jordan types (P, Q) that arise from multiplication by two linear forms ell_1 and ell_2 on an algebra A with H(A) = H?
accepted.context_brief: Pairs of Jordan types in codimension two

evidence.quote: Question 5.9. In [10], all possible linear Jordan types of complete intersection algebras of codimension two having a fixed Hilbert function is listed. For every such Hilbert function H, can we determine the pairs of Jordan types P and Q that occur for (ℓ1, A) and (ℓ2, A) where H(A) = H?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 3.5. Study Togliatti-type varieties and their companion surfaces for other root systems and find a Togliatti-type construction associated to configurations of points allowing multiple general fat points as described in [44].

evidence.quote: Problem 3.5. Study Togliatti-type varieties and their companion surfaces for other root systems and find a Togliatti-type construction associated to configurations of points allowing multiple general fat points as described in [44].

This direction of study has been pursued in [20] in case of Togliatti-type varieties and their companions associated to the B4, F4 and H3 root systems and to certain Fermat-type configurations of points.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 5.6. If the Artinian algebra A is Gorenstein, can we always find a pre Jordan basis B that agrees with the Q(a) decomposition, in the sense that B ∩ m^i ∩ (0 : m^b) is a basis for the vector space m^i ∩ (0 : m^b) for every i and b?

evidence.quote: Question 5.6. If the Artinian algebra A is Gorenstein, can we always find a pre Jordan basis B that agrees with the Q(a) decomposition, in the sense that B ∩ mi ∩ (0 : mb) is a basis for the vector space mi ∩ (0 : mb) for every i and b?
The next question has to do with the symmetric decomposition of the associated graded algebra of a non-graded Gorenstein Artinian algebra (see [28]).

trace.notes: Mapped a 14-page paper titled "List of Problems". Major blocks are Section 2 on failure/presence of Lefschetz properties for special algebras, Section 3 on geometric aspects, Section 4 on combinatorics, and Section 5 on Lefschetz properties and Jordan types. Open-problem regions are dense in pages 2-12 and are explicitly labeled as Question, Problem, or Conjecture.

Extracted 12 explicit open items from the special-types-of-algebra block: Questions 2.1-2.3, Conjecture 2.4, Questions 2.5-2.10, Problem 2.12, and Question 2.13. Excluded Conjecture 2.11 because the paper states it has already been solved.

Extracted 9 explicit open items from the geometric-aspects block: Questions 3.1-3.4 and 3.9, plus Problems 3.5-3.8. Marked Problem 3.5 for review because the available local evidence does not fully define the paper-specific terms needed for a standalone rewrite.
Extracted 6 explicit open items from the combinatorics block: Problems 4.2-4.4 and 4.7, plus Questions 4.5 and 4.6.

Extracted 9 explicit open items from the Jordan-types block: Questions 5.1-5.9. Marked Question 5.6 for review because the Q(a) decomposition is referenced but not defined in the locally available evidence.
